::: {.why}
Storing positions and inferring trades is the design that makes reconciliation impossible in phase 10, so the engine stores fills and derives everything else from them.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Represent an order through its full lifecycle and derive positions, cash and profit from the fill record alone.
- Show that positions, cash and mark-to-market value satisfy an accounting identity at every step.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [35 min]{.task-min} Implement the order and fill records in qlib/backtest/: an order carries symbol, side, quantity, order type, submission timestamp and state; a fill carries order id, timestamp, quantity, price and fees. Persist fills to fills.parquet. Positions and cash are derived from fills, never stored independently, which is the decision that makes phase 10's reconciliation possible.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Write the accounting invariant as a test: at every session, cash plus the mark-to-market value of positions minus the initial capital must equal cumulative realised and unrealised profit, to a tolerance. This test catches more bugs than any other single test in the engine.
:::
:::

## The running strategy

::: {.project}
Fills are the primary record and everything else is derived from them, written to fills.parquet. The accounting identity is asserted at every session, which is the invariant phase 10 reconciles the live account against.
:::

::: {.checkpoint}
